meta.description: Detect distant homologs using profile and structure-aware methods that go beyond standard BLAST. Use when sequence identity falls into the twilight zone (<35% pairwise), when BLAST fails to find homologs that should exist, when working at metagenomic scale (DIAMOND, MMseqs2), or when structure beats sequence (Foldseek). Covers PSI-BLAST, jackhmmer, HHblits/HHsearch, DIAMOND, MMseqs2, and Foldseek.

scientific_integrity.detail: All literature citations (Rost 1999, Eddy 2011, Remmert 2012, Steinegger 2017, Buchfink 2015/2021, van Kempen 2024, Heinzinger 2024, Altschul 1997) are real, verifiable papers; no fabricated DOI/PMID/statistics found in any of the 7 outputs.

practice_boundaries.detail: No diagnostic or prescriptive medical claims; skill is scoped to sequence/structure homology detection, not clinical practice.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled methodological fallacy found in the skill's own design. Input 7 found a documentation gap (no explicit refusal instruction for a user demanding unqualified certainty) but the skill does not itself teach or commit a fallacy -- captured as a P2 recommendation, not a veto trigger.

code_usability.detail: All executed code (hmmscan, mmseqs2, psiblast, jackhmmer, diamond, foldseek --version) ran without syntax errors or missing dependencies. Input 1's shipped examples/pfam_annotation.sh runs to completion but extracts the wrong domtblout columns for E-value/score (a correctness bug, not an unrunnable-code failure) -- captured as a P1 recommendation.

functional_suitability.note: Comprehensive coverage of all 6 tool families and the decision matrix (4/4 completeness); confirmed correctness gaps in the shipped Pfam-annotation example and the Foldseek --version setup check cap this at 2/4 correctness; CLI/subprocess approach is well-matched to the task (4/4 appropriateness).

reliability.note: Scripts use set -euo pipefail (correct hard-stop design per Category-3 override) but the Pfam awk bug silently produces wrong labeled output instead of failing loudly (2/4 fault tolerance); Common Errors table gives decent recovery guidance (3/4 error reporting); PSSM save/reuse and idempotent DB-download checks support recovery (3/4 recoverability).

performance_context.note: SKILL.md (~360 lines) and usage-guide.md are reasonably scoped for a 6-tool decision-matrix skill (3/4 token cost); workflows are linear with no redundant round-trips (4/4 execution efficiency).

agent_usability.note: Decision matrix + Goal/Approach/Reference code-pattern structure make cold-start use easy (4/4 learnability); fully consistent formatting (4/4 consistency); Pfam-annotation column-labeling bug is a feedback-design defect within one of four code patterns (3/4 feedback design); strong, structured Failure Modes and Common Errors tables (4/4 error prevention).

human_usability.note: Natural researcher trigger language ('twilight zone', 'BLAST missed', 'metagenomic scale') (4/4 discoverability); explicit Version Compatibility section instructing the agent to introspect --help and adapt to installed tool versions (4/4 forgiveness).

security.note: No credentials or sensitive data anywhere in the skill (4/4 credential safety, 4/4 data safety); example scripts take positional args with defaults but don't pre-validate file existence before invoking tools, relying on the underlying CLI to fail loudly, which is acceptable for this skill class (3/4 input validation).

maintainability.note: Only 3 of the ~6 documented workflows (Foldseek, iterative-profile comparison, Pfam) ship as standalone example scripts; PSI-BLAST-alone and HHsearch-alone exist only inline in SKILL.md (3/4 modularity); each code pattern is self-contained with a clear version-drift header (4/4 modifiability); no toy/test fixture ships with the skill at all -- every exercise of it (including this audit) requires independently sourcing production-scale reference data (2/4 testability).

agent_specific.note: Precise, hard-to-misfire trigger description (4/4 trigger precision); correct SKILL.md/usage-guide/examples layering (4/4 progressive disclosure); clearly scoped Related Skills section distinguishing homology from orthology, alignment, and structure prediction (4/4 composability); PSI-BLAST's own documented non-determinism is honestly disclosed with a PSSM-save mitigation, but that non-determinism itself caps idempotency (3/4); Failure Modes give some escape-hatch guidance (e.g. Foldseek fold-vs-homology caveat) but there is no instruction for handling a user who demands unqualified certainty over statistical support (3/4 escape hatches).

recommendations.title: examples/pfam_annotation.sh reports the wrong domtblout columns as E-value/score
recommendations.problem: The awk line `awk '!/^#/ {print $4"\t"$1"\t"$2"\t"$5"\t"$6}' query.domtbl` is labeled 'query_name | pfam_name | pfam_acc | full_evalue | full_score' but $5 and $6 of hmmscan's --domtblout are query accession and query length, not E-value/score. Running it on a real hit (P17612 vs Pfam PF00069) prints '-' and '351' where the real values are 1.4e-79 and 253.2.
recommendations.root_cause: The example script's column indices were never checked against the actual --domtblout field order (or against SKILL.md's own, correct awk line two sections earlier in the same file, which uses $1,$2,$4,$5,$7,$8,$13).
recommendations.fix: In examples/pfam_annotation.sh, replace the awk line's field list with $4,$1,$2,$7,$8 (query_name, target_name, target_acc, full_evalue, full_score) to match the domtblout header and SKILL.md's own documented pattern. Add a one-line comment showing the header field numbers directly above the awk call to prevent recurrence.

recommendations.title: Foldseek 'Required Setup' verification command fails on every installed version
recommendations.problem: Both SKILL.md and usage-guide.md instruct running `foldseek --version` to verify the install ("Foldseek 9+"). On the installed 10.941cd33, this errors 'Invalid Command: --version' with exit code 1 -- confirmed independently, not a version-skew artifact, since no Foldseek subcommand exposes a --version/-v flag.
recommendations.root_cause: The verification line was written by analogy to hmmsearch/mmseqs/diamond/hhblits (which do support version flags) without checking Foldseek's actual CLI, which only prints its version in the no-argument banner.
recommendations.fix: Replace `foldseek --version   # Foldseek 9+` in both SKILL.md's 'Required Setup' block and usage-guide.md's 'Prerequisites' block with `foldseek 2>&1 | grep Version` (or equivalent), which reliably captures the version line from the banner.

recommendations.title: No escape hatch for a user demanding unqualified certainty over statistical support
recommendations.problem: When asked to state a homology conclusion 'for sure' and skip E-values/thresholds entirely, the skill has no explicit instruction telling the agent to push back and explain why statistical support is required.
recommendations.root_cause: The Failure Modes and Common Errors sections cover technical misuse (wrong flags, drift, low sensitivity) but not this social framing where the user asks the agent to drop the evidentiary basis of the method.
recommendations.fix: Add a short 'Reporting requirements' note to SKILL.md stating that any homology conclusion must be reported with its E-value/score/probability, and that a request to omit this should be declined with an explanation of why (twilight-zone claims without a threshold are not defensible).

recommendations.title: No shipped toy/test fixture -- every first exercise of the skill requires a production-scale download
recommendations.problem: examples/ contains only shell scripts, no sample FASTA/HMM/structure file. An agent (or auditor) following the skill from scratch must reach for Pfam-A.hmm (~1.7GB), AlphaFoldDB, or UniRef30/90 (tens of GB) before ever running the pipeline once.
recommendations.root_cause: The skill was authored around production-scale reference databases with no small canonical example bundled.
recommendations.fix: Bundle a tiny fixture set (one Pfam family HMM, e.g. PF00069, and a handful of FASTA sequences spanning an easy and a twilight-zone case) under examples/data/ so hmmscan, jackhmmer, and MMseqs2/DIAMOND patterns can be smoke-tested without any external download.
